scope: Non-operational computational analysis of an already-public longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 cohort. No pathogen engineering, wet-lab protocol, clinical recommendation, or treatment claim.

meta_registry_transfer.question: Does an orthogonal infectious-virus state carry correctness-relevant successor information that a current PCR snapshot plus phase coordinate does not encode?

target.known_measurement_boundary_from_public_a: Negative CN values are encoded as 48, saliva Ct as 47, and negative culture as Virus_pos_days=5.9.

exposure_boundary.already_seen_before_freeze: Header, four exemplar data rows, and authors' public R code describing field meanings and their published figure analyses.
not_done_before_freeze: No model A/model B comparison computed.
No threshold selected from predictive results.
No search for the exact claim that culture time-to-positivity predicts next-day PCR conditional on current PCR and phase.

claim.IF: two observations share the same modeled PCR-state variables but differ in infectious-virus culture state
claim.UNDER: subject-held-out prediction of the next exact-day nasal PCR transition with current nasal PCR and time-from-nasal-peak already provided
claim.THEN: adding current viral-culture time-to-positivity will improve out-of-subject prediction of next-day nasal CN
claim.BECAUSE: infectious-virus state may encode productive-infection information not contained in RNA burden plus phase alone
claim.UNLESS: culture state is merely redundant with current PCR/phase or the public sampling design does not identify the incremental information

eligibility: same subject has finite Nasal_CN at exact Time=t and exact Time=t+1
current row at t has finite Virus_pos_days
current Nasal_CN < 48 and next-day Nasal_CN < 48 so the primary continuous transition is not an encoded PCR non-detection boundary
no interpolation or nearest-neighbor time matching
endpoint.baseline_model_A: ordinary least squares fitted only on training subjects: delta ~ intercept + current_Nasal_CN + Time
endpoint.enriched_model_B: same OLS model plus current Virus_pos_days
endpoint.cross_validation: leave-one-subject-out; every prediction for a subject is produced by a model trained on all other eligible subjects only
endpoint.primary_metric: MAE across all held-out eligible transitions

frozen_pass_fail.EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT: fewer than 30 eligible transitions or fewer than 10 held-out subjects, or intermediate result not meeting PASS/FAIL

permutation_null.operation: For each iteration, permute Virus_pos_days across eligible current rows globally, rerun the exact same leave-one-subject-out enriched model, and compute relative MAE gain versus the unchanged baseline model A.
permutation_null.purpose: Test whether the culture feature adds more held-out prediction than an equally-shaped but relationship-destroyed feature. This is a dataset-specific randomization test, not a universal causal p-value.

secondary_cross_modal_endpoint.outcome: next-day saliva Ct transition among rows with finite uncensored saliva Ct at t and t+1
secondary_cross_modal_endpoint.interpretation: Concordant information gain in saliva would be cross-modal support inside the same cohort, not independent replication.

if_PASS_then_required: independent external cohort with serial PCR plus infectious-virus measurement
material consequence analysis showing why the extra state changes model/measurement interpretation
